# Environment Setup {#sec-setup}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Appendix status: drafted.** Versions here are the ones the book's
measurements were actually run with, so that a chapter's numbers are
reproducible rather than approximately reproducible.
:::

Everything in this book runs in one of three places:

- **Your browser.** Every interactive widget is self-contained — nothing to
  install, nothing to run.
- **A Python environment.** Every measurement in this book was run on **Python
  3.14.5**. Anything from 3.11 will run the code; only 3.14.5 is the version the
  numbers came from.
- **A local model server.** Parts IV–VII call a model. Every measurement in
  those parts used `ollama` on a laptop rather than a hosted API, so that the
  numbers cost nothing to reproduce and do not depend on a provider's current
  model version.

## Local setup {#sec-setup-local}

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-chapters.txt
```

Or with `uv`, which is faster and — because every line is pinned with `==` —
resolves exactly the same versions:

```bash
uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -r requirements-chapters.txt
```

::: {.column-margin}
The repository also has a `requirements.txt`, and it is a different thing: the
handful of packages that render the book. Installing that one will not give you
the chapter code.
:::

Below is what `requirements-chapters.txt` pins. Each version is the one a
chapter's own *"The stack these numbers came from"* table reports, and where two
chapters disagree both are shown, because that disagreement is a fact about the
book rather than something to average away.

Two packages that used to be in this table are not measurement dependencies and
have been moved out: `matplotlib` and `jupyter` render the book rather than
produce any number in it.

[Pin these rather than taking latest.]{.hl} Several of the book's findings are
about specific tool behaviour — @sec-summarization's ROUGE tokenizer bug,
@sec-turkish-nlp's lowercasing failures — and a newer version may have fixed
the very thing a chapter is demonstrating. That is a good outcome for the world
and a confusing one mid-exercise.

## Accelerators {#sec-setup-gpu}

`pip install torch` resolves to a different wheel on every platform, and the
fine-tuning chapters produce slightly different numbers on different backends.
The book's fine-tuning and embedding measurements ran on **Apple Silicon
through PyTorch's MPS backend** — four chapters say so in their own version
tables — so that is the configuration the numbers came from.

- **Apple Silicon.** `pip install torch` is enough; MPS is built in. Setting
  `PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1` avoids a hard failure on the few operations
  that still have no MPS kernel.
- **NVIDIA.** Install the CUDA wheel explicitly rather than letting `pip`
  choose, or you may silently get the CPU build:
  `pip install torch==2.13.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126`.
- **CPU only.** Everything runs. The fine-tuning chapters take several times
  longer, and nothing else changes.

Expect small numerical differences across backends. If a fine-tuning result in
@sec-sequence-labeling or @sec-machine-translation is a point or two from the
book's, the backend is the first thing to check and usually the whole answer.

## A local model {#sec-setup-ollama}

Parts IV–VII need a model to call. Install [ollama](https://ollama.com), then
pull the models the chapters you want actually used:

```bash
ollama pull qwen3.5:9b        # ~6 GB   — most of the book's measurements
ollama pull llama3.2:3b       # ~2 GB   — the small-model rows and the serving chapters
ollama pull gemma3:27b        # ~17 GB  — needs roughly 20 GB of memory
ollama pull qwen3.6:35b       # ~21 GB  — needs roughly 24 GB of memory
ollama pull nomic-embed-text  # ~0.3 GB — the gateway chapter's embedding path
ollama serve
```

The book used `ollama` 0.24.0. Which model a chapter used is in its status
callout, and the distribution is lopsided:

| model | chapters that measured with it |
|:--|:--|
| **`qwen3.5:9b`** | 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 29, 30, 38 — the default, and the one to pull first |
| `llama3.2:3b` | 12, 18, 31, 33, 34, 38 |
| `gemma3:27b` | 12, 14, 21, 22, 38 |
| `qwen3.6:35b` | 7, 12 |
| `qwen2.5:7b` | 35, 36, 38 |
| `nomic-embed-text` | 32 |

: Which chapter needs which model {tbl-colwidths="[24,76]"}

If memory is tight, pull the first two and skip the rest: every chapter that
uses a large model also reports a smaller one, and the arguments survive without
the top rung — @sec-multimodal and @sec-llm-eval say so explicitly.

Everything talks to the HTTP API directly:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate \
  -d '{"model":"qwen2.5:7b","prompt":"Merhaba","stream":false}'
```

::: {.column-margin}
Two flags worth knowing before you debug something for an hour. `"format":
"json"` forces parseable output and removes a whole class of scoring bug. And
`"think": false` matters for reasoning models — without it, `ollama` returns an
empty `response` with the content in a separate `thinking` field, which scores
as zero and looks like a catastrophic quality result. @sec-governance's
measurement hit exactly that.
:::

## What this costs in disk and memory {#sec-setup-budget}

Worth knowing before the first `pull` rather than after.

| you want to run | disk | memory |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Parts I–III (no model server) | ~4 GB | 8 GB |
| Everything with `qwen3.5:9b` | ~10 GB | 16 GB |
| Adding `gemma3:27b` | ~27 GB | 20 GB+ |
| Adding `qwen3.6:35b` as well | ~48 GB | 24 GB+ |

: Budget before you start {tbl-colwidths="[52,24,24]"}

Memory here is what the model needs resident, and on a unified-memory machine
that is the same pool your editor is using. @sec-serving explains why the
number that actually binds is the KV cache rather than the weights, and why the
context length you configure is a memory decision.

## Colab {#sec-setup-colab}

Colab is the shortest path to a GPU for the fine-tuning chapters, and the
notebooks are not published yet — the badges are on the roadmap rather than in
the book, so for now copy the code blocks. The local-model chapters do not work
on Colab's free tier without adaptation; substitute a hosted API and expect your
numbers to differ from the book's, which is itself a useful lesson about
pinning.

## Windows {#sec-setup-windows}

Everything works; three things differ.

Activate the virtual environment with `.venv\Scripts\activate` rather than
`source`. Use **WSL2** if anything fights you — the book's measurements were run
on macOS and Linux, and WSL2 is the shortest path to matching them. And set
`PYTHONUTF8=1`, because Windows still defaults some file reads to a non-UTF-8
encoding, which mangles Turkish text silently. That last one is
@sec-turkish-nlp's argument arriving before you have even loaded a model.

## Getting help {#sec-setup-help}

Open a GitHub issue with the chapter name in the title. If a number in the book
does not reproduce, that is worth an issue — say which chapter, which package
and model versions you have, which accelerator backend, and what you got. The
first three are usually the answer.
